object.title: The Horse Fair
object.pick_reason: The artist Rosa Bonheur famously obtained a police permit to dress in men's clothing so she could sketch anonymously at Parisian horse markets for this monumental masterpiece.

title_options: She Had to Break the Law to Paint This
The Secret Disguise Inside This Massive Painting
Why the Police Let This Woman Wear Pants
metadata.description:
Rosa Bonheur went to extreme lengths to paint "The Horse Fair" in 1850s Paris, including securing a special police permit to dress like a man. Watch to see how she snuck herself right into the middle of the action!

metadata.pinned_comment: If you had to wear a disguise to get into an exclusive event today, what would you dress up as? Let me know in the comments!

script: She wore pants illegally just to paint this. To paint "The Horse Fair" in the 1850s, Rosa Bonheur had to get an official "cross-dressing permit" from the Paris police. Seriously, back then women weren't allowed to wear trousers, but Rosa needed to blend into the chaotic, muddy, male-dominated Parisian horse markets to sketch. And look at the payoff! The energy here is absolutely wild. You can practically hear the hooves thundering and feel the dust kicking up. Look at this guy in blue trying to hold back a rearing black stallion, or these massive percherons charging right at us. Rosa spent over a year working on this massive, sixteen-foot canvas. But here is my favorite detail: right in the middle of all this testosterone and horse sweat, look at this figure in the blue cap looking straight at us. Yep, that's Rosa herself, hiding in plain sight, casually riding among the men. She basically crashed the boys' club, made an absolute banger, and became an international superstar. Would you go to this length for your art?
